request: How does active sticky or snapshot-v1 state behave across a full dynamic Client restart?
answer: snapshot-v1 restores an exact checkpoint; sticky requires an identity-bound fail-closed or reset-on-restart disposition, and reset completes before runtime availability.

sticky.identity: state_restart_disposition is part of the canonical graph digest
sticky.fail_closed: Client keeps the runtime unavailable while the control connection remains usable
sticky.reset_on_restart: Client invokes reset-state-v1, validates the exact state schema, health-checks the graph, then reports runtime availability

snapshot_v1.identity: wasmc.dynamic-lib-state-checkpoint/v1 binds graph revision, graph digest, block schema and state digests
snapshot_v1.proved: SV2:2 survives full Client restart and receipt recovery without replay; post-migration SV3:2 survives on the target schema

host_boundary: reset-state-v1, snapshot-v1 and restore-v1 are opaque Lib operations over the unchanged resource/window/operation/completion boundary; fixed Host API and minimal CLI are unchanged.
not_claimed: sticky state preservation when reset-on-restart is selected
